claims.statement: The wiki tree has two distinct names: the OpenWiki CLI hardcodes `openwiki/` as its output directory in the workspace (declared as `NATIVE_WIKI_DIR` in `app/services/wiki_runner.py`, imported by `packer.py` and `publisher.py`, the only modules that actually move the tree), while `Settings.wiki_artifact_dir` (env `WIKI_ARTIFACT_DIR`, default `.openwiki`) only renames the packaged output and the committed root. `pipeline.py` never names the native directory: it threads `settings.wiki_artifact_dir` into `adopt_hidden_wiki`, `pack_wiki(root_name=...)` and `publish_wiki(artifact_dir=...)`.

`Settings.wiki_artifact_dir` is validated to be a simple folder name - non-empty, not `.` or `..`, and containing no `/` or backslash - because the value becomes a path component in the zip and a pathspec in `git add`; an invalid value fails Settings construction.

`JobStore` is the sole owner of the per-wiki workspace paths: `job_dir` = `<DATA_DIR>/jobs/<wiki_id>/`, `repo_dir` = `.../repo/` (which contains the `openwiki/` tree), `logs_path` = `.../logs.txt`, `wiki_zip_path` = `.../wiki.zip`, and `meta_path` = `.../job.json` (legacy only). `wiki_id` is validated against a 32-hex pattern and `jobs_dir` is created in `__init__` so the API and workers can race to create it safely.

Deleting a wiki removes both its database row and the entire `<DATA_DIR>/jobs/<wiki_id>/` directory, so the workspace artifacts and the packaged zip are reclaimed together (also driving `purge_expired` retention).

`openwiki/.run.json` is the CLI's durable, transient resume state that this service never writes. `wiki_runner.read_run_state` parses it into `{phase, total, completed, pending, current}` by counting `plan.pages[*].status == "complete"`, tolerating a missing, unparsable or malformed file by returning `None` or a zeroed summary.

The worker's `_track` task polls `read_run_state` every `WORKER_PROGRESS_SECONDS`, formats the result with `format_progress` into the job's `progress` column (`"2/7 pages - generating"`), and falls back to `packer.count_pages` (a `**/*.md` count under `openwiki/`) when no plan is available.

The push-back commit excludes the transient `openwiki/.run.json` state while including the wiki's versioned evidence: the `git add` pathspec is `--all --force -- <artifact_dir> :(exclude)<artifact_dir>/.run.json`, so `.openwiki/.run.json` and the scaffolding outside the wiki folder (e.g. `AGENTS.md`) are absent from the remote tree while `.openwiki/index.md` and `.openwiki/.claims/*` are present.

`adopt_hidden_wiki(repo_dir, artifact_dir)` renames a wiki shipped as the artifact directory (e.g. `.openwiki/`) to the CLI's hardcoded `openwiki/`. It is a no-op when `artifact_dir == "openwiki"`, when `openwiki/` already exists, or when the artifact directory is not a directory; the pipeline runs it immediately after the fetch and before `decide_mode`, so an adopted hidden wiki correctly resolves to `--update` instead of `--init`.

`publisher._expose_artifact_dir` performs the reverse rename of the workspace's `openwiki/` to `WIKI_ARTIFACT_DIR` inside `publish_wiki`, after packaging. It raises `PushError("openwiki/ directory is missing; nothing to push")` when `openwiki/` is absent, returns immediately when the artifact dir is `openwiki`, and otherwise deletes any pre-existing `<artifact_dir>/` tree (logging `replacing the existing ... tree`) before renaming, so stale pages are not merged into the source repository.

Pipeline ordering keeps the two transformations apart: adoption happens before the CLI run, `pack_wiki` reads `openwiki/` next, and the rename to `WIKI_ARTIFACT_DIR` happens last in the optional push block. This is why a failed push still leaves a valid, downloadable `wiki.zip`.

`packer.pack_wiki(repo_dir, dest_zip, *, root_name=NATIVE_WIKI_DIR)` zips the workspace's `openwiki/` tree with every entry rooted at `root_name` (`WIKI_ARTIFACT_DIR` in production), counts `.md` files as `pages`, returns `(pages, size_bytes)`, writes to `dest_zip + ".tmp"` and then atomically replaces the target, and raises `PackError` when `openwiki/` or `openwiki/index.md` is missing so no partial wiki is advertised.

A `--depth 1` clone does not contain the commit recorded in `openwiki/.last-update.json` (`gitHead`), so `ingestion.ensure_full_history` runs `git fetch --unshallow` before an `update` run; without it, an incremental `--update` would diff against an empty history.

`wiki_runner.prepare_instructions(repo_dir, language)` writes `openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md` only when a language is requested and the source does not already ship one; a user-authored brief always wins and no language means no file. The file is part of the wiki tree, so it appears both in `wiki.zip` and in the pushed commit.

`openwiki/.claims/` holds the versioned Claim evidence committed with the wiki and shipped inside `wiki.zip`, and `openwiki/.page-manifest.json` is OpenWiki's per-page provenance bookkeeping. Both are CLI-owned outputs that the service only carries through packaging and push - the test fixtures fabricate `.claims/`, `index.md` and `.last-update.json` to exercise exactly that path.

The packaged zip is served by `GET /wikis/{wiki_id}/download` as `openwiki-{wiki_id}.zip` with `404` while the artifact is not yet ready, and its entries are rooted at `WIKI_ARTIFACT_DIR` (e.g. `.openwiki/index.md`) in both git and upload runs.

`Settings` derives the three storage paths the workspace depends on: `data_dir` defaults to `/data` in containers and `./data` on Windows local development; the `jobs_dir` property is `data_dir / "jobs"` (mirroring `JobStore.jobs_dir`); and the `resolved_config_dir` property is `openwiki_config_dir` when set, otherwise `data_dir / ".openwiki-config"`. `resolved_config_dir` is CLI state (credentials, install id) exported as `OPENWIKI_CONFIG_DIR`, not wiki content, so it must not be confused with the `WIKI_ARTIFACT_DIR` default `.openwiki` that lives inside a repository workspace.

The two renames form a round trip that makes retries resumable: `_expose_artifact_dir` is the last step of the pipeline that mutates the workspace, so it leaves `<artifact_dir>/` where `openwiki/` used to be; on a retry or requeued claim `_fetch` short-circuits on the surviving `.git` directory and nothing recreates `openwiki/`, so the mirrored `adopt_hidden_wiki` call at the start of the next attempt is what restores the layout the CLI requires.

Staging with `git add --all --force -- <artifact_dir> ...` has two behavioural consequences beyond the `.run.json` exclusion: `--all` follows the workspace state, so because `openwiki/` is replaced onto the artifact directory rather than merged, paths deleted by a regeneration are staged as deletions and disappear from the commit; and `--force` is required because the conventional root `.openwiki` is a dot-directory that plain `git add` skips (and that a source repository may list in `.gitignore`).

The coordination database `<DATA_DIR>/openwiki.db` is a sibling of the `jobs/` directory inside the single `Settings.data_dir` root: `JobStore.__init__` sets `jobs_dir = data_dir / "jobs"` (creating it), sets `db_path = data_dir / "openwiki.db"` and opens that SQLite connection with WAL enabled, so both the API and the worker containers share one file plus one `jobs/` tree on the mounted volume.
